detectors.title: Explore detectors
detectors.spectrumDescription: Nominal SPHEREx wavelength bands from 0.75 to 5 micrometers, with 17 channels per detector. Widths are proportional to wavelength intervals. Illustrative colors progress from violet at shorter wavelengths to golden orange at longer wavelengths; this is not calibrated per-pixel coverage.
detectors.help: Each segment loads the latest observation of this region from that detector; its date may change. Illustrative colors follow wavelength from violet to golden orange, not real colors or intensities. Ranges are nominal: the actual wavelength varies across each detector.
detectors.empty: No observation was found for the requested detector. The previous image is retained.

appearance.failed: The requested processing was not applied. Original data are displayed.
appearance.legend: Displayed intensity scale: low to high

compare.noData: An image has no valid pixels to display. Review processing or choose another observation.
compare.yearScope: Observations of this region across the selected year, from January through December (UTC).
compare.yearSearching: Searching {{year}} for observations of this region… This may take a while.
compare.yearTooBroad: Too many observations matched this region and year to complete the calendar. Try a specific detector or another year. Available dates could not be confirmed.
compare.yearCancelled: The yearly search was cancelled. Your added images are retained.
compare.searchWait: Querying the IRSA archive… This may take a few seconds.
compare.empty: No other observations were found for this year and detector. Try another year or any detector.
compare.limited: Only the 100 most recent matching observations from this year were retrieved. More results exist outside this list; select a detector to narrow the search.
compare.draft: Updating observations for the selected year. Added images are retained.
compare.startSearch: Choose a year to find observations of this region.
compare.chronological: Plays from oldest to newest. A remains the reference.
compare.needPartner: Search and add another observation to start blinking. You can keep adding more.
compare.incompatibleUnit: This observation has a different unit from A or does not specify one. It was not added to the comparison.
compare.units: Units are missing or different. Comparison requires compatible units.
compare.position: All images need a current position before comparison.
compare.processing: Wait for processing of the images to finish.
compare.busy: Wait for the current operation to finish.
compare.invalidYear: Select a mission year from 2025 through the current year.

projection.refining: Loading a new cutout for this zoom…
projection.refineFailed: The new cutout could not be loaded. The previous image is retained.

help.observationDate: When the satellite acquired this observation, in UTC. This is independent of the sky clock. During comparison it identifies the visible image.
help.release: The archive data release in IRSA, such as DR1 or QR3. This is the actual provenance of the loaded observation.
help.basic: Information about image size and data availability that does not require technical knowledge.
help.technical: Coordinates, units and file references for closer inspection. Statistics describe the original data.
help.dimensions: Columns and rows in the native-resolution cutout. It may be rectangular near an exposure edge; framing preserves the complete image.
help.size: Requested angular side of the cutout, in arcminutes. The available file may cover only part of that size.
help.coverage: Percentage of pixels with finite numeric values in the original file. This is not a quality measure and does not include flag filtering.
help.requested: Right ascension and declination of the requested point, in ICRS degrees. These describe a sky position, not the observer's terrestrial location.
help.center: Center of the actual cutout. It may differ from the requested point near an exposure edge.
help.unit: Intensity unit in the original file, usually MJy/sr. Signal-to-noise mode produces unitless values.
help.dtype: Original numeric type: float32 or float64. The display copy retains the dimensions and is normalized for the GPU.
help.range: Minimum and maximum finite values in the original image. Display contrast uses percentiles, so these extremes alone do not determine appearance.
help.observation: Archive-provided exposure identifier, used to distinguish observations and trace their origin.
help.headers: WCS relates image pixels to sky coordinates. These cards come from the original file and include its distortions.
help.visual: These settings adjust the display. During comparison they apply equally to all images, with one shared scale.
help.palette: Maps measured intensity to tones. False color is not an RGB photograph and cannot directly determine composition.
help.exposure: Visual adjustment in EV steps: +1 increases brightness and −1 reduces it. Original scientific data are preserved.
help.opacity: Image transparency over the sky. At 100% its full intensity is shown; lower values reveal the background.
help.processing: These options request processed values from the API and apply consistently to all images in the comparison. The first request may download extra planes.
help.mask_flags: Hides pixels rejected by the file's quality flags. Missing data remain transparent even when this option is off.
help.subtract_zodi: Subtracts the file's zodiacal-light model, which may reduce background differences between observations.
help.signal_to_noise: Divides values by the estimated noise deviation. The result is dimensionless and should not be interpreted as MJy/sr intensity.
help.comparison: Drag the timeline or use its arrow keys to explore the added observations from oldest to newest. Manual movement pauses playback. Play advances the same timeline automatically. A remains the reference and cannot be removed. Images stay aligned by sky coordinates, with their own geometry. A visual difference alone does not confirm motion or variability.
help.criteria: A's detector is selected by default. A shared detector helps with an initial comparison but does not guarantee the same wavelength at each pixel. Changing this criterion does not remove images you already added.
help.candidates: Choose a year from the start of the mission in 2025 through the current year. The list searches this region and detector across the entire year, retrieving up to the 100 most recent matching observations. A and observations from its exact time are excluded from the comparison list. Searches retrieve metadata only; pixels are downloaded when you add an observation. Added images are retained when you change years.
help.interval: How long each image stays visible, from 0.1 to 3 seconds. Playback uses loaded images without downloading them again.
